X.note: Real archival aerial shot of a barge in a canal lock. The sepia grain suits the 1957 newsreel, and the caption states place and date plainly. The lower gradient keeps the white text legible. The footage is soft, and the caption is a bit small for a phone. The source line is dimmer and thinner than the caption.

Y.note: Sharp, well-lit modern drone shot of Chicago-area neighborhoods with a lake horizon. It looks better than X. The caption text sits over bright rooftops and trees, and the gradient is weak, so contrast is lower than in X and the line is harder to read. The caption asks 'works that way?' with no visible referent, so the picture doesn't show what 'that way' means. The generic stock footage is labelled 'illustrative'. The source line is small and low in contrast.

why: X's footage matches its caption and has stronger text contrast, while Y has nicer footage but a caption that refers to something the frame doesn't show and is harder to read over the busy rooftops.
top_fix_for_weaker: Strengthen the dark gradient behind the caption, or put it on a solid translucent bar. Enlarge the source line. Rewrite the caption so it names the subject (for example, 'Chicago neighborhood zoned for single-family and two-flat homes, today'), so the frame carries its own meaning.
